newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi promises welfare reform by Jan 1998.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi promises welfare reform by Jan 1998.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi, responding to criticism of Italy's recent budget action, promised on Thursday to introduce a structural reform of the welfare state by the beginning of next year.
"We have said that we will have completed a reform of the welfare state by January 1, 1998 after wide-ranging talks open to everyone," Prodi told a rally in this central Italian town.
"By January 1 we will have a structural transformation," he added.

The European Commission and International Monetary Fund warned Italy this week that it had introduced too many one-off budgetary measures in its bid to be ready for the 1999 launch of the single European currency.
The IMF called on Prodi to introduce "structural cost-saving measures" to ensure the sustainability of state accounts.
Prodi told the Lucca rally ahead of Sunday's local elections that he would improve the welfare state.
"We will be careful to cut waste and pay attention to the most needy," Prodi said.
Talks with unions over welfare reform are due to start before the middle of next month, but agreement between all the various parties will be hard to achieve.
The hard-left Communist Refoundation, which secures Prodi's majority in the lower house of parliament, has already ruled out any cuts in welfare spending.
